independent_acceptance_review.scope: Independent acceptance of all three reported findings, their quantitative and zero-measure repairs, and the stated dimension-one/local proof corrections. The current root read the complete 709-line report, complete findings and coverage, and the cited decisive source pages; the original full-paper reading is retained as historical coverage, not repeated or relabelled as current work.

findings.reason: The truncated flat tori have exactly the common admissible local constants alpha=pi and Lambda=1 and diameter 1. Truncation changes no small-diameter Hausdorff covers. The half-cylinder has sides 2L and outer content 8, so every permitted dilation of B(p,2)=X forces C>=L/32. This disproves uniform dependence, not existence for a fixed space. If the auxiliary proof requires radius<2D, B(p,3/2) supplies the same whole-space witness. No diameter-scale upper bound can be silently inserted into the printed definition.

For diag(100,100,1)S^2 with chordal distance, the two Lipschitz comparisons give the stated Ahlfors bounds for all radii, while contraction of the inverse small cap works for every center and every r<D/200=1. Both signed unit graph disks lie in B(p,3) with area>=pi; negative points of 6B have |z|>49/50 and therefore cannot enter E_t for t<49/50. The content is exactly zero. The one-integer constancy inference on a disconnected target is invalid. Adding A0 alone does not cure it.

The global datum A0 yields doubling 2^n max(alpha^2,A0 alpha,1), including r=D by comparison with D/2. The working q=Lambda R or 3D/2 has q<2D, places the target in one connected open component of B(2q), and gives 6q<=9Lambda R. Repeating the filling/slicing construction at q while retaining B0 in the two final volume terms legitimizes a single integer. The smallness budgets keep U outside 4Bq and the final cover outside 2Bq where required; n=2 zero-cycle augmentation is compatible. Large-content and positive-delta small-content branches cover P0=0. Monotonicity of localized content gives the stated dilation. External weak-Poincare characterization remains a named dependency.

An infinite zero-H1 Cantor set in the n=2 case makes equation (4.1) force identity into a finite zero-complex. The topological-dimension bound instead allows Z=S, identity/inclusion and a constant homotopy. This handles the exact endpoint without refuting Lemma 4.2.

The homotopy mass estimate must use mass(S), not the zero mass of S'. Proposition 5.9 derives full support from pushforward independently of the lower-density proposition, so the n=1 nonzero augmentation-zero slice has mass at least 2 without circularity. Integrating and extending gives the stated lower bound. Weak (1,1) plus truncation of an L1 gradient gives k*measure{h>k}->0; it does not assert a false strong-L1 maximal theorem. The good-set distance bound then gives uniform convergence and mass-tail control. These local repairs and the stated external-version limitations are consistent; they do not establish blanket correctness of all external theorems.
